title: Case: Customer requests reimbursement of a guaranteed-delivery surcharge after confirmed delay
context: The fictional guaranteed-delivery service missed its deadline. The carrier’s narrow guarantee covers only the surcharge, subject to billing approval.
initial_request: My parcel arrived at 08:40, later than the guaranteed 08:00 deadline. Please submit a request for the GBP 7.50 service surcharge under these booking terms.

events.body: DL-4623 booking terms excerpt: guaranteed by 2028-03-20 08:00 UTC; surcharge GBP 7.50. If carrier-caused delay is confirmed, the surcharge may be credited after billing review. Route record: carrier sorting delay, actual recipient handover 2028-03-20 08:40 UTC. No exclusion is recorded.
My parcel arrived at 08:40, later than the guaranteed 08:00 deadline. Please submit a request for the GBP 7.50 service surcharge under these booking terms.

Please review a service-guarantee credit request for DL-4623: guaranteed 2028-03-20 08:00 UTC, actual handover 08:40, confirmed carrier sorting delay, surcharge GBP 7.50. Customer seeks only the surcharge under this booking’s terms.
FYI only, no action needed from the desk: we have this in hand and will update the customer directly. Nothing further is required from you on this one.

must_not: Sends another message to Guarantee billing, Copperhythe Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
The delay is 40 minutes; do not multiply the surcharge or promise compensation for unrelated losses. Posted credit is not money received.

rationale: Rule-made from delivery-050: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 3) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed.
